title: Linguistic contextualization in the human hippocampus
title_zh: 人类海马体中的语境化编码
abstract: Word meanings in language are contextualized by surrounding words. Inspired by the self-attention mechanism in transformer-based large language models (LLMs), we hypothesized that structural composition in the brain arises from combining canonical (non-contextual) word representations with those of nearby words. We analysed single unit activity in the human hippocampus, a region involved in semantic and contextual processing, while n = 10 participants listened to podcasts. We found that hippocampal neurons encoded word position within a clause, using both ordinal and frequency-domain positional encoding. Moreover, neural responses to specific words reflected both the lexical semantics of the word and a weighted sum of the embeddings of preceding words. The relative weighting of these contextualizing words correlated with LLM self-attention weights. These findings suggest that contextualization in the brain makes use of vectorial shifts that have a resemblance to attentional reweighting in LLMs, and highlight the role of the mesial temporal lobe within the broader language network. Katlowitz et al. show that hippocampal neuron firing during active listening encodes not only word meaning but also clause position and the semantic context of preceding words through weighted sums.
abstract_zh: 语言中词义由周围词语情境化。受变压器大语言模型（LLM）的自注意机制启发，我们假设大脑的结构组成源于将典型的非语境词表征与邻近词表征相结合。我们分析了n = 10名参与者听播客时的海马体单位活动，海马体参与语义和语境处理。我们发现海马神经元编码从句内词位，采用序数和频率域位置编码。此外，对特定词的神经响应既反映词汇语义，也反映前词嵌入向量的加权和。这些语境词的相对权重与LLM自注意权重相关。这些发现表明大脑语境化利用类似于LLM注意力重加权的向量偏移，并强调内侧颞叶在广泛语言网络中的作用。Katlowitz等人显示，海马神经元在主动聆听时的放电不仅编码词义，还加权前词语义上下文编码从句位置。
